> Many have stated, or implied, that Ted is an anarchist.  It should be noted,
> though, that he had no pretentions of being an anarchist.  In fact, he only
> dedicated a very small paragraph in his Manifesto to describe the
> motivations of an anarchist.   In addition, in the paragraph above in which

> description of anarchists may resonate with how he feels, if he were an
> anarchist he would have made it very clear from the beginning of his
> Manifesto.  I think it would be fair to say that there are basic
> psychological elements that he shares with anarchists.

	In a letter to the New York Times, received April 24, 1995, the
Unabomber offers a self-identification as "FC" a "group of anarchists." 
Responding to a letter-to-the-editor, FC subsequently acknowledged that
other anarchists and ecologists would not approve the use of violence. 
Also, the program of ISAIF (breaking society down into isolated
individuals and very small groups) is intrinisically anarchist. 
Finally, they discuss cases of revolution that are often invoked by
anarchists as examples of a good try being hijacked by leftist fanatics.
